Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

Face — her own: a cool, aloof beauty; fair skin; oval face; medium-sized eyes — wide almond eyes, level outer eye corners; thin straight brows; straight narrow nose; thin lips with a defined cupid's bow; pale silver eyes with a fine steady ring of yellow light; glossy nude lips.

Her element, carried in her design: ytterbium: a soft, ductile, bright silvery metal named for the Swedish village of Ytterby, separated in 1878 in Geneva from erbia, with its younger sister lutetium still hidden inside it until 1907; held one by one in an egg-crate lattice of light, its atoms tick to a steady yellow laser more than five hundred trillion times a second in optical clocks so exact they would not lose a second over the age of the universe and can feel time run faster when lifted a few centimetres, the likely successor to the caesium second; squeezed hard, its electrical resistance rises, so it gauges the pressure of earthquakes and blasts; inside glass fibre it powers the invisible infrared lasers that cut steel.

3. COSTUME — FANTASY
Costume: a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns.
Silhouette: a floor-length priestly vestment with gold-trimmed stoles and a tall head ornament — a long, devout silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: bright soft silver, steady clock-laser yellow, faint deep-red lattice glow, clear night blue.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE

Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Yb) and atomic number (70) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, corset, bustle, Victorian tailoring, modern material, machinery.
